chain.title: A change after issue shows
chain.text: Every document carries a SHA-256 fingerprint of its content and the fingerprint of the previous document, sealed with an HMAC. If someone alters an issued document, the chain after it stops matching.

why.title: Why EN 16931 now
why.p1: A PDF invoice is a picture of the data. The recipient's software cannot read the total or the VAT from it without text recognition. A structured document carries the same data in named fields: BT-1 is the number, BT-2 is the date, BT-3 is the document type.
why.p2: According to the bill as introduced, mandatory structured e-invoices between companies and to the state start on 1 July 2028. Many invoicing programs today produce only PDF, without structured XML. The documents you issue in Fakturist now are already in these formats.

1.a: The European standard for the content of an electronic invoice. It defines which data an invoice holds and what the fields are called, for example BT-1 for the number and BT-2 for the date. Fakturist saves every document under it, in UBL 2.1 and CII.

2.q: Is Fakturist approved by the National Revenue Agency?
2.a: No. No such approval exists today. According to the bill as introduced there will be accredited providers and certified software, with the conditions set in an ordinance that is not out yet. When they are published, we will say so here.

3.q: What does the free plan include?
3.a: One company and one user, the VAT checks and EN 16931 XML. There is a soft monthly limit on documents: a document is always issued, and above the limit we invite you to choose a paid plan.

4.q: Does my customer get a PDF?
4.a: Yes. Every document is issued as structured XML (UBL 2.1 and CII) and as a PDF copy with Cyrillic. If your customer is also on Fakturist, the document lands in their inbox on its own, with an email carrying the PDF and XML. Sending over the e-invoicing network is coming and is not offered as ready.

5.a: On servers in the European Union. For the data in our customers' invoices we act as processor under Art. 28 GDPR, on your instructions.

einvoicing2028.title: E-invoicing in Bulgaria from 2028: a guide for companies
einvoicing2028.summary: According to bill no. 52-602-01-60 amending the VAT Act, as introduced, structured e-invoices become mandatory between companies and to the state from 1 July 2028. The invoice will be a document in UBL 2.1 or CII under EN 16931, not a PDF. The bill has passed only a first reading, on 12 November 2026, so the text may change.

q1.title: What does the bill provide?
q1.p1: The bill provides for mandatory structured e-invoices between companies (B2B) and to the state (B2G) from 1 July 2028. They will travel over the CEF eDelivery AS4 network in UBL 2.1 and CII under EN 16931.
q1.p2: The issuer will send the invoice only to the recipient's address in the register the bill creates. There will be accredited providers and certified software. The conditions for them will be set in an ordinance.

q2.title: What are the dates?
q2.p1: The dates below follow the text as introduced. The ordinance is not out yet, so its deadline is a provision, not a fact.

q3.title: What is a structured e-invoice?
q3.p1: A structured e-invoice is a document in which every item of data sits in a named field that software can read without text recognition. A PDF is not such a document: it displays the data, it does not describe it.
q3.p2: The EN 16931 standard gives every field a code. Here is an excerpt of an invoice in UBL 2.1, with the field codes in the left column:
q3.bt1: Invoice number. Ten digits, no gaps (Art. 114(1)(2) VAT Act).
q3.bt3: Document type. 380 is an invoice, 381 is a credit note.

q4.title: What happens to the recipient?
q4.p1: According to the text as introduced, the recipient loses the input VAT credit if there is no structured e-invoice. So it is not only issuers who need to be ready: companies that only receive invoices will also want the documents in this form.

q5.title: How will the invoice be sent?
q5.p1: The issuer will send only to the recipient's address in the register the bill creates, over the CEF eDelivery AS4 network. The details of the register and of the providers will be in the ordinance. Those conditions are not published yet.

q6.title: What is still unclear?
q6.p1: The ordinance with the conditions for accredited providers and certified software is not out yet. According to the text as introduced, its deadline is 1 July 2027. No approval from the National Revenue Agency exists today, and Fakturist does not claim one. Nor do we claim to meet requirements that have not been set.

q7.1: Check your numbering: ten digits and no gaps. Art. 114(1)(2) of the VAT Act already requires it.
q7.2: Ask your accountant and your software provider whether they will issue UBL 2.1 or CII, not only PDF.
q7.3: Keep counterparty data accurate: company ID, VAT number and address. A structured document carries them in separate fields.
q7.4: Follow the ordinance and the text at the second reading. The conditions for providers and software will decide what is needed.
q7.title: What should a company do now?

q8.title: What does Fakturist already do today?
q8.p1: Every document is issued as both UBL 2.1 and CII under EN 16931, the free plan included. Not available yet, but planned: {planned}.
